caption:
When you're stressed, how do you speak to yourself?

Self-compassion means meeting your own hard moments with the kindness you would give a friend. A meta-analysis of trials found programmes that taught it over several weeks were linked with less stress than having no programme. They did about as well as other approaches, like relaxation training, not better, and many of the studies had quality problems.

Many of these programmes used a short practice called a self-compassion break:
1. Name it. "This is a hard moment."
2. Remember you're not alone. Other people feel this too.
3. Offer yourself a kind word, the way you would a friend. "What do I need right now?"

This is a taster, and the programmes ran for weeks. If self-criticism feels heavy, talking it through with a psychologist is an option.

Save this for a hard day.

Research:
Han, A., & Kim, T. H. (2023). Effects of self-compassion interventions on reducing depressive symptoms, anxiety, and stress: A meta-analysis. Mindfulness, 14(7). https://doi.org/10.1007/s12671-023-02148-x

This content is for general informational purposes and does not constitute psychological advice. If you are experiencing significant distress, please speak with a registered health professional.
